reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module that constructs an alebrije blending jaguar and eagle traits, with a hybrid body and wings painted in vivid Oaxacan-style dots, swirls, and zigzags, aiming for a moderate-sized, well-structured implementation using only reliable SDK calls.

I'm sketching the skeleton layout, placing hips, spine, chest, neck, and head along a forward-facing axis, then working out custom paint functions that layer bright base colors with dotted rosette patterns and cycling hues to achieve the alebrije look.

Rather than one continuous skinned mesh, I'll go with separate overlapping sweeps for spine, tail, and neck, letting rounded caps hide the seams where they meet. I'm sketching the spine as a catmull curve from the hips joint curving up and forward toward the chest, with the hips chain parented accordingly.

I'll build a three-joint spine chain (spine1-3) parented to hips, then sweep a body tube along it using a radius function that varies elliptically to give the jaguar a deeper chest at the front.

Next I'm adding a neck chain of two joints curving up and forward from the end of the spine, parented to the last spine joint.

Then I'm shaping the eagle's head and neck ruff: a feathered collar around the neck, with the head joint placed at the neck's end and the skull built as a scaled sphere.

For the beak, I'm sweeping a hooked cone shape with taper for the upper beak, and a separate sweep attached at a jaw joint for the lower beak, using the head's local forward/up/left coordinate helper to position everything relative to the head's orientation.

Now I'm working out the skeletal joints: confirming that model-left corresponds to +X, setting up the head joint parented to the neck's last chain point with proper direction, and defining the jaw joint positioned slightly below and forward of the head using the local offset helper.

I'm placing a sphere mesh for the skull, scaled anisotropically along world axes since the head has no extra orientation, giving it width, height, and length proportions roughly facing +Z. I'm also planning crest feathers or plume blades at the back of the head for the eagle's head detailing.

Still writing feather outline...

I'll reuse a handful of paint variants across feathers to limit bake cost, and now I'm designing the wings as an arm chain per side—shoulder, elbow, wrist joints positioned out and back in a spread rest pose using two catmull spans per wing.

For the flight feathers, I'm planning to extrude primaries along a fan from the wrist and secondaries along the forearm, attaching each feather to the arm chain's bone at a given parameter point.

Working out secondary feathers and coverts next, placing them along the forearm with shallower angles and shorter lengths, then layering smaller covert feathers on top slightly raised. I'm figuring out the perpendicular axis so each feather lies flat in a roughly horizontal plane rather than standing vertically.

I'm planning the feather layout in three layered rows: flight feathers (primaries and secondaries), then greater coverts shifted and shorter, then lesser coverts shorter still and more colorful, each offset slightly upward and positioned at the leading edge. That gives roughly 96 feather parts total across both wings once doubled for symmetry.

Now mapping feather bases along the arm chain from shoulder to wrist, varying each feather's angle so secondaries sweep from about 110° near the shoulder to 75° near the wrist, then primaries continue outward from 10° to 68°. Checking the resulting wingspan, it comes out around 3.1 meters total, which is oversized for a 1.4m jaguar body but acceptable for a fantasy creature.

Scaling down instead: positioning the wrist closer at 0.7 with shorter primaries gives a more reasonable 2.4m total wingspan, so I'm redefining the shoulder, elbow, and wrist joint positions with the wing lifted and feathers offset upward slightly. I'm also placing a rounded shoulder joint where the wing mounts to the back, checking it sits correctly relative to the body's torso height, and now I'm setting up the four legs with root and foot target positions for front and hind limbs.

Working through the leg rigging now, I'm deciding on bend directions and segment lengths so the front legs bend their elbows backward while the hind legs bend knees forward in a more natural cat-like stance, checking the vertical reach of each chain against the target foot height. I'm also planning the paws as flattened spheres with small toe spheres and bright claw accents to match the alebrije style, and starting to name the leg bone chains.

Defining limb radius tapers...

legs; hind legs parent to the hips root joint near the back of the body. For the tail, I'm planning a long jaguar-style tail that transitions into a feathered fan like an eagle's, chained outward from the hips.
